cards.text: This is a song of David, Israel's king, written for the choirmaster. David is crying out to God. Pull up a stool, friend.

cards.question: David is crying out to God in a song for the choirmaster. What does he ask for first?

answers.text: That God hurry to help him
That God show him the way to go

cards.text: “Hurry, O LORD, to help me!” is the prayer version of mashing the elevator button five times, and honestly, I RESPECT it. Then David turns to the people who seek his life.

cards.question: David prays that the people who seek his life will end up ashamed.

cards.text: Then there are the ones who say, “Aha, aha!” That's the sound of somebody LAUGHING while you drop a whole tray of cookies, and David prays they retreat because of their shame.

cards.question: David turns from his enemies to a different crowd: everyone who seeks God. What does he want for them?

answers.text: That they rejoice and be glad in God
That they hide until the danger passes
That they march out and fight beside him

cards.text: Then David says, “But I am poor and needy…” and this is the KING of Israel. Meanwhile I put on one clean apron and strut around like I'm royalty.

cards.question: David calls himself poor and needy, but he says God is his help and his ___.
David closes Psalm 70 by telling God to take His time.

cards.text: Psalm 71 is a new psalm, and its writer isn't named. He opens with, “In You, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.”

cards.question: The writer asks God to rescue and deliver him. What does he appeal to?

cards.text: He asks God to be his refuge, a place he can always go. Not a place with business hours, friend. ALWAYS.

cards.question: The writer asks God to give the command to save him. What does he call God?

cards.text: He asks God to deliver him from the hand of the wicked, the unjust and ruthless. Then he calls God his hope and his confidence, and he starts looking back over his life.

cards.question: Looking back over his life, the writer says he has leaned on God since his ___.

cards.text: He says he has become a portent to many, but God is his strong refuge.

cards.question: All day long, the writer's mouth is filled with God's ___.

cards.text: Now the writer prays about getting older: “Do not discard me in my old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.” Friend, I got shoved to the back of a junk drawer the day a shiny new stamper showed up, so I'm over here nodding SO hard my hat's about to fall off.

cards.question: The writer's enemies are plotting against him. What do they say about him?

cards.text: And they keep going. They say, “…pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him.”

cards.question: With his enemies saying no one will rescue him, the writer asks God not to be far from him.

cards.text: He prays, “Hurry, O my God, to help me.” Then he says may his accusers be ashamed and consumed, and may those who seek his harm be covered with scorn and disgrace.

cards.question: With accusers all around, the writer says he'll go quiet and wait it out.
The writer says he'll tell of God's righteousness and salvation all day long. What does he admit about them?

answers.text: He can't know their full measure
He has only seen them once
He has forgotten most of them

cards.question: The writer says he'll come in his own strength.

cards.text: He'll proclaim God's righteousness, and he adds, “Yours alone.” God has taught him from his youth, and to this day he's still telling of God's marvelous deeds.

cards.question: The writer asks God not to forsake him, even when he's old and gray. Until what?

answers.text: Until he tells the next generation of God's power
Until every one of his enemies is gone
Until he gets to see his home once more

cards.text: He wants to tell God's might to all who are to come. Most folks pray for retirement, but this man is praying for OVERTIME.
Then he looks UP and says God's righteousness reaches to the heavens, and God has done great things. Friend, my tallest cookie stack barely reaches my hat.

cards.question: Thinking of the great things God has done, the writer asks God a question. What is it?

answers.text: How long will this go on

cards.text: Then he gets honest: God has shown him many troubles and misfortunes.

cards.question: Though God has shown him many troubles and misfortunes, the writer says God will ___ him once again.

cards.text: Even from the depths of the earth, he says, God will bring him back up.

cards.question: The writer says God will increase his honor and comfort him once again.
The writer says he'll praise God with the harp and the lyre. What does he praise God for?
When the writer sings, his lips shout for joy along with his soul, which God has ___.

cards.text: He wraps up by saying his tongue will proclaim God's righteousness all day long. That's because those who seek his harm are disgraced and confounded.
